title: AVX2 probe reads 32 bytes from argv storage
reasoning: The program treats argv[argc-1] as a 32-byte __m256i input and performs an unbounded 256-bit load from it. When executed, argv[argc-1] can be argv[0] or a short argument string, so the load can read past the argument object's bounds and invoke undefined behavior or crash under sanitizers/hardened runtimes. The file appears intended as an instruction availability check, so it can exercise AVX2 without depending on process argument storage.
recommendation: Use a fixed local 32-byte buffer with known contents, then load from that buffer before calling the AVX2 intrinsic.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and nothing in the excerpt exercises execution with short or absent user arguments.
suggestedRegressionTest: Compile and run the probe under AddressSanitizer with no extra arguments and with a one-byte argument; it should exit without out-of-bounds reads.
minimumFixScope: Change main to load from a local 32-byte array instead of argv[argc-1].
